title: Comment on: “Ten-year-plus follow-up study on coronectomy of the mandibular third molar—methodological considerations and future directions”
html: We congratulate Li and Leung on their valuable contribution to the long-term safety profile of mandibular third molar coronectomy1. Their 10-year prospective cohort demonstrates a 15.2% reoperation rate with no nerve deficits following reoperation, supporting coronectomy as a nerve-preservation strategy when mandibular third molars are in close proximity to the inferior alveolar nerve (IAN). Recent reviews have confirmed the favourable outcomes of coronectomy, with IAN injury rates ranging from 0.55% to 0.76%2,3, substantially lower than the 1.04% nerve deficit rate reported for conventional extraction at the authors’ institution.
